claims.explanation: Triclabendazole is a microtubule inhibitor that also binds DNMT1, and its selective killing pattern is best explained by dependence on microtubule dynamics and DNA methylation maintenance rather than by any single lineage. Lines with TP53 loss combined with intact RB1 and activating KRAS/BRAF/PIK3CA signaling are enriched among sensitive lines, whereas mesenchymal/NF1- or NF2-mutant lines and several EGFR-mutant lung lines are relatively protected. High expression of tubulin/microtubule machinery and DNMT1 would be expected to sensitize, while low expression or efflux/EMT programs would protect.

KRAS-mutant gastric, colorectal, ovarian, pancreatic and lung lines are enriched among sensitive lines
BRAF-mutant melanoma and colorectal lines appear among the most-killed lines
PIK3CA-mutant gastric and colorectal lines are enriched among sensitive lines
RB1 loss co-occurs with TP53 mutation in several highly sensitive lines
microtubule inhibitor mechanism; high beta-tubulin expression increases target availability
annotated triclabendazole target; high DNMT1 expression increases dependence
NF1-mutant thyroid sarcoma, upper aerodigestive and glioma lines are among the least affected
NF2-mutant ovarian, pancreatic and soft-tissue lines are relatively resistant
EGFR-mutant lung lines appear in both sensitive and resistant groups, but several resistant lung lines carry EGFR mutations
SF3B1-mutant kidney and lung lines are among the least affected
CDKN2A-mutant melanoma and bone lines are relatively resistant
